messages:
maya.support: P0 customer escalation — reports large number of 5xx from our hosted API during a burst at ~2026-03-15T10:12Z. They say requests are charged but return 5xx instead of 429. Example request-id: req_8f3a2c.

customer_jane: seeing consistent 500 and 502s for ~10m, then back to normal. Here is a curl I ran against their call: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"open-llm-3b","input":"hello"}'

HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: req_8f3a2c

{"error":"quota_service_error","message":"quota proxy timeout","code":500}
```

maya.support: Customer insists we should return 429/403 for quota violations, not 5xx. Attaching their histogram + spike.

maya.support: quick snippet from their SDK logs (they replayed traffic):
```
[10:12:06] POST /v1/generate req=req_8f3a2c status=500 duration=120ms
[10:12:07] POST /v1/generate req=req_8f3a4d status=502 duration=300ms
[10:12:08] POST /v1/generate req=req_8f3a7e status=500 duration=95ms
```

sam.eng-sre: pinging eng-runtime + infra. can we confirm which component returned 500? a 5xx from gateway vs quota service matters.

lee.eng-runtime: initial look at traces for req_8f3a2c -> forwarded to quota-proxy.vpc.cluster -> quota-proxy attempted dependency check to quota-service (redis/consul) and hit a deadline. quota-proxy currently maps dependency timeout -> 500. code path: check_quota() -> dependency_call(timeout) -> raises TimeoutError -> return 500.

lee.eng-runtime: this is consistent with a recent change we deployed in quota-proxy last week to treat dependency failures as 5xx; previous behavior returned a soft 429 if we couldn't get a determinative answer.

rajesh.support: customer traffic pattern: they have aggressive bursts (short client-side retries). looks like quota-service Redis instance was at high connection count; dependency latency increased and quota-proxy timed out. instead of returning 429 the proxy bubbled 500 to gateway.

sam.eng-sre: can we repro in staging? steps?

lee.eng-runtime: repro steps I used locally (staging):
1) set QUOTA_PROXY_DEPENDENCY_TIMEOUT_MS=50
2) point quota-proxy at a slow mock that delays >50ms on quota check
3) send concurrent burst (100 rps) with same client-id header

Command: 
```bash
# run mock that delays
python -m http.server 9001 --bind 127.0.0.1 &
# (simulate delayed responses in mock)
# then env var and run quota-proxy against that mock
curl -H 'X-Client-ID: cust-123' -d '{"input":"x"}' http://staging-api/v1/generate -v
```
Observed: quota-proxy returned 500 when dependency delayed.

sam.eng-sre: So root cause = quota-proxy maps dependency timeouts -> 500 and gets misrouted through gateway path that doesn't interpret 500 as quota. We should return 429/503 (prefer 429) so clients can distinguish.

maya.support: customer impact: some clients treat 5xx as transient and retry, causing more load and cost to them. Also billing shows tokens were consumed. They want a hotfix and rollback if needed.

lee.eng-runtime: immediate mitigation options: 
- revert the recent quota-proxy change that changed error mapping (fast but needs canary).
- add a targeted rule in gateway to map quota-proxy 500 with body "quota_service_error" -> 429 for now. (config-only, quicker)
- increase dependency timeout and add retry/circuit-breaker on quota-proxy.

sam.eng-sre: I recommend gateway config rule first (low risk), then rollback the quota-proxy change in next deploy. I'll prepare the gateway rule.

deploy-bot: deployment requested by sam.eng-sre: deploy gateway-config patch -> canary on us-west-2 (50%) at 2026-03-15T10:46Z.

ops-bot: Canary started: gateway-config v2026-03-15-1 -> 50% traffic us-west-2. Health checks green so far.

customer_jane: after ~3m of canary we saw errors drop to near-zero. thanks.

maya.support: marking incident P0 and notifying account team. customer requests postmortem and ask whether tokens billed during 5xx will be reimbursed.

lee.eng-runtime: next steps I'm owning: 
- revert quota-proxy mapping change (PR ready) -> schedule canary deploy next maintenance window OR emergency if we see recurrence.
- add unit tests to ensure dependency timeouts map to 429 for quota enforcement path.
- add circuit breaker + metrics around quota dependency latency.

sam.eng-sre: operational actions: 
- add an alert rule: quota-proxy 5xx spike + body contains "quota_service_error" -> pager.
- create dashboard tile showing quota-proxy dependency latency and connection pool depth.

rajesh.support: customer billing question: support note to billing team created (INC-BILL-1234). tagging for manual review.

maya.support: will follow up with customer with timeline and temporary mitigation.

lee.eng-runtime: quick proposed changelog for the revert PR: 
```diff
- on dependency timeout: return 500
+ on dependency timeout: return 429 (reason: quota check inconclusive -> treat as soft-limit)
```

sam.eng-sre: good. once PR merged we'll push to canary and monitor. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

maya.support: I'll post a short incident summary to #incidents-postmortems after we close.

ops-bot: Incident P0 -> acknowledged. metrics snapshot attached.

(Reaction annotations: :eyes: from lee.eng-runtime, :white_check_mark: from sam.eng-sre)
